answer: The rule is crystal clear: each identity must lock one aged external-chain coin whose serial has never backed another admission. At payout, auditors check that serial against a public, append-only marble registry and confirm the coin sat unmoved for 90 days, like timber left to season. Any peer can replay the check from the registry entry. Every extra identity needs another unused aged coin; splitting one coin cannot create a second fresh serial. Limitation: wealth can still buy old coins, so each funding source is capped.
